ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the graph of the quadratic function $y=ax^{2}+bx-3$ intersects the x-axis at points $A(-1,0)$ and $B(3,0)$, and intersects the y-axis at point $C$. The vertex of the parabola is point $M$. Point $P$ is a point on the parabola, with the x-coordinate of point $P$ being $m$ ($m>3$). Point $Q$ is on the axis of symmetry, and $AQ \perp PQ$. If $AQ=2PQ$, find the value of $m$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw a line parallel to the x-axis passing through point Q, intersecting the line parallel to the y-axis passing through point P at point N, and intersecting the line parallel to the y-axis passing through point A at point M.\\
$\therefore \angle AMQ=\angle QNP=90^\circ$\\
$\therefore \angle QPN+\angle PQN=90^\circ$\\
$\because \angle AQP=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle AQM+\angle PQN=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle AQM=\angle QPN$,\\
$\therefore \triangle AMQ\sim \triangle QNP$.\\
$\therefore \frac{AM}{QN}=\frac{MQ}{NP}=\frac{AQ}{QP}=2$.\\
The axis of symmetry of this parabola is the line $x=1$,\\
thus let the coordinates of point Q be (1, t),\\
given that the coordinates of point P are ($m$, $m^{2}-2m-3$),\\
hence $AM=t$, $QN=m-1$, $MQ=2$,\\
$NP=t-m^{2}+2m+3$.\\
$\therefore \frac{t}{m-1}=\frac{2}{t-m^{2}+2m+3}=2$.\\
Solving, we get $m=0$ (discard) or $4$.\\
Therefore, $m=\boxed{4}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, the parabola opens upward, A is the intersection point with the x-axis on the left side, B is the intersection point with the x-axis on the right side, C is on the negative half-axis of the y-axis, and the vertex M is below; the dashed vertical line is the axis of symmetry of the parabola, Q is located on this dashed axis of symmetry, P is located on the right branch of the parabola, and line segments AQ and QP are connected. Then reason: from the two x-axis intersection points -1 and 3, and the constant term -3, one may set y=a(x+1)(x-3). Substituting the constant term gives -3a=-3, so a=1, therefore y=x^2-2x-3, and the axis of symmetry is x=1. Let Q=(1,t), P=(m,m^2-2m-3), and m>3. A=(-1,0), so slope(AQ)=t/(1-(-1))=t/2. Also slope(QP)=(m^2-2m-3-t)/(m-1). Because AQ perpendicular PQ, [t/2]*[(m^2-2m-3-t)/(m-1)]=-1. In terms of distance, AQ^2=(1+1)^2+t^2=4+t^2, PQ^2=(m-1)^2+(m^2-2m-3-t)^2; from AQ=2PQ, obtain 4+t^2=4[(m-1)^2+(m^2-2m-3-t)^2]. To solve the equations, let d=m-1, then d>2, and the y-coordinate h of P is h=m^2-2m-3=d^2-4. Vector AQ=(2,t), vector QP=(d,h-t). Perpendicularity and AQ=2PQ are equivalent to vector QP being in a perpendicular direction to vector AQ and having length half of it, therefore there may be (d,h-t)=(t/2,-1) or (d,h-t)=(-t/2,1). The first case gives t=2d, h=t-1=2d-1, thus d^2-4=2d-1, namely d^2-2d-3=0, giving d=3 or d=-1; because d>2, take d=3, so m=d+1=4. The second case gives t=-2d, h=t+1=-2d+1, thus d^2-4=-2d+1, namely d^2+2d-5=0, whose solutions do not satisfy d>2. Therefore the unique value satisfying m>3 is m=4.
